title: Ashtpadi 23, salok: the ointment of wisdom
hookLine: giaan anjan gur deeaa: the Guru gave the ointment of wisdom and the darkness went (Sukhmani 23)

cards: In many Punjabi homes, there's a small bottle or a little metal pot of surma, a fine dark powder for the eyes.

A grandmother might line a baby's eyes with it, or her own, with a thin stick, an old custom across South Asia. People say it cools the eyes and protects them. Gurbani's word for eye-ointment like this is anjan.
And the twenty-third ashtpadi of Sukhmani opens with the Guru putting anjan on someone's eyes.

teach.b: The salok, in paraphrase: the Guru gave the ointment of spiritual wisdom, and the darkness of ignorance was destroyed. By God's grace I met the holy one, and Nanak's mind was lit up. Take it in pieces.
Giaan is wisdom, especially the kind that knows God. Anjan is the eye-ointment, the kohl or surma. So giaan anjan is wisdom pictured as a balm for the eyes.

teach.h: GUR DEEAA: THE GURU APPLIES IT.
teach.b: And notice who applies it: gur deeaa, the Guru gave it. You don't put it on yourself. Then the result: agiaan andher binaas.
Agiaan is not-knowing. Andher is darkness. Binaas means destroyed, gone.

teach.h: THE DARKNESS ENDS, LIKE SHUTTERS OPENING.
teach.b: The darkness isn't argued away; it simply ends, the way a dark room ends when someone opens the shutters. The second line says how: har kirpaa, by God's grace, the seeker met the holy one.
And the last word is pargaas: light, the mind lit from within. Look at what ointment actually does. It doesn't add anything new to the world.
The trees, the faces, the sky were all there already. It just lets you see them.
That's how Sikh teaching often talks about the Guru's wisdom: not information piled on top of life, but clearer eyes for the life already in front of you.
Over the next days, the ashtpadi shows what those cleared eyes see.

how: Sikhs reciting Sukhmani Sahib's twenty-third ashtpadi begin with a salok picturing the Guru's wisdom as anjan, eye-ointment, that ends the darkness of ignorance.

o: secret knowledge kept for a chosen few
a medicine said to cure blindness
wisdom pictured as a balm for the eyes

s: in the salok, the seeker applies the ointment alone
gur deeaa: the Guru gave it.
anjan is the same kind of eye-ointment as surma or kohl
a dark powder used across South Asia, said to cool and protect the eyes.
the salok says wisdom adds new things to the world
like ointment, it lets you see what was already there.

games.q: the room of your mind is dark. in the twenty-third salok, how does the darkness end?
o: you argue it away, point by point.
the Guru applies the ointment of wisdom, and it's simply gone.
you wait for it to fade on its own.
games.why: gur deeaa, the Guru gave it, and agiaan andher binaas: the darkness of ignorance was destroyed, by God's grace.

practice: If you can, cup cool water in your hands and bring it gently to your closed eyes two or three times, then dry them slowly and sit, eyes closed, as the coolness fades.
When you're ready, open them slowly and let the first thing you see simply be there. If you pray, say Waheguru as you open your eyes.

wordCard.voice: Giaan anjan, the eye-ointment of wisdom: the Guru gave it, and the darkness of ignorance was gone.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: anjan, eye-ointment or kohl; giaan anjan is the eye-ointment of wisdom.

carryVoice: Your line: the guru cleared my eyes. Nothing new added, only seen. Five hundred twenty-six days, and counting.

sources.ref: Sukhmani Sahib, ashtpadi 23, salok (Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 293)
